title: Electron lattice potentials for ultracold atoms using circular Rydberg orbitals
authors: Aileen A. T. Durst, Einius Pultinevicius, Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Tilman Pfau, Matthew T. Eiles, Florian Meinert
abstract: Recent advances in experiments using individually trapped atoms have enabled precise control over circular Rydberg electrons with exceptionally long lifetimes. We show that these giant and stable electron orbits can form toroidal lattice potentials for ultracold atoms with a period set by the electron's de Broglie wavelength. Unlike conventional static optical lattices, this electron lattice is formed via the electron-atom interaction, which mixes Rydberg circular states with opposite azimuthal phase winding into a standing electronic matter wave. The lattice phase is thereby intrinsically coupled to the atom position. For a pair of atoms, this results in ballistic tunneling motion in the two-atom spatial correlations along the ring, while the single particle dynamics is essentially free rotation. We simulate the dynamics for an experimentally realistic setting that exploits optical tweezers for individual atom control. Our results open a route toward incorporating long range atom-atom interactions mediated by a single electron and, ultimately, realizing small Bose and Fermi gases confined in these microscopic electronic atom traps.
summary: The authors demonstrate how circular Rydberg electrons can generate a dynamic, standing-wave lattice potential for ultracold atoms. This lattice potential is formed by the electron's matter wave and couples the atomic degrees of freedom. The study predicts correlated tunneling dynamics, opening a pathway to engineer complex many-body interactions in quantum gas experiments.
main_problem: To realize and investigate an electronic lattice potential for ultracold atoms, where the lattice is formed dynamically by the matter wave of a weakly bound electron, rather than being a static optical lattice.
main_result: The system exhibits correlated tunneling motion in the electronic lattice, where individual atoms behave as free rotors, but the relative motion is governed by the lattice potential.
method: The dynamics are analyzed by deriving an effective low-energy angular Hamiltonian and solving the resulting Bloch Hamiltonian in momentum space.
model_or_system: The system involves ultracold atoms interacting with a single electron prepared in a circular Rydberg state, forming an effective electronic lattice potential via the electron-atom interaction.
key_observables: Band structure $E_{\pm}(q; K)$, effective moment of inertia ($I^*_\Phi, I^*_\varphi$), and two-atom correlation functions ($P_{com}, P_{rel}$).
important_parameters: Electron-atom scattering length ($a_s$), Rydberg principal quantum number ($n$), and the ratio $J/V \sim n m_e / m_a a_0$.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the Born-Oppenheimer approximation by averaging over fast radial and axial oscillations, and assumes the azimuthal motion is slow.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the electronic standing wave and resulting single/two-atom potentials, the band structure $E_{\pm}(q; K)$ showing tunneling parameters, and the time evolution of two-atom correlators after a quench.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the effective angular Hamiltonian from the full trimer Hamiltonian, analyzing the resulting band structure for relative motion, and finally simulating the time evolution of two-atom correlations after switching off the trapping potential.
why_interesting: This work provides a novel mechanism for creating tunable, dynamic lattice potentials using highly excited Rydberg states, offering a platform to study long-range, electronically mediated atom-atom interactions.
